meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'badly'.
Secondary conversational sense ('it's bad') (predicative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to speak, to talk') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
goes right before the word it negates
not to be confused with есть 'there is' (from быть)

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'fish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'normal' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('decent, OK') (colloquial) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Declinable masculine noun meaning 'coal', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: We grilled the meat over charcoal.

examples.text: А зачем идти за дровами? Я вот уголь взял.
examples.trans: And why go for firewood? I brought charcoal right here.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to drink', forming an aspectual pair with 'выпить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
used on its own: он пьёт = he drinks

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('uh-huh') used directly in spoken exchanges.
Secondary conversational sense ('yeah, right') (said ironically) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Yeah, right, like with the Cayenne?

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'pack, packet' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Для этого крема нам понадобятся две пачки сливочного масла.
examples.trans: For this cream we will need two packs of butter.

examples.text: На столе лежала открытая пачка крупной морской соли.
examples.trans: An open packet of coarse sea salt lay on the table.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ожрать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'devour, gobble up'.

examples.text: Кто опять успел сожрать все свежие круассаны до открытия?
examples.trans: Who managed to devour all the fresh croissants before opening again?

examples.text: Голодный пёс за секунду сожрал целый кусок дорогой вырезки.
examples.trans: In a second the hungry dog gobbled up a whole piece of expensive tenderloin.

meanings.note: + genitive: ни копейки = not a penny
Secondary conversational sense ('...  = neither... nor') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'horseradish; hell (colloq.)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Подай к холодному мясу свежую горчицу и острый хрен.
examples.trans: Serve fresh mustard and spicy horseradish with the cold meat.

examples.text: Какого хрена вы стоите без дела в разгар ужина?
examples.trans: What the hell are you standing around idle for in the middle of dinner?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'be sick, ache'.

examples.text: Я этого не хочу. Но вспомни, у тебя сын болеет.
examples.trans: I don't want that. But remember, your son is ill.

meanings.note: у меня болит живот = I have a stomach ache
у меня болит живот = I have a stomach ache

examples.text: Живот у тебя, как у депутата.
examples.trans: You've got a belly like a member of parliament.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'it is necessary'.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: 'пойдём' / 'пойдёмте'; colloquially also 'пошли'

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'home'.

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: And you go home and do your homework.

examples.text: Так, мы идём к слепым. А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: Right, we're going to the blind people. And you go home and do your homework.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'пойти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('expression') (to run for a second term) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

отдыхать.gloss: to rest, to relax, to vacation

meanings.en: to rest, to take a break
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дыхать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to rest', forming an aspectual pair with 'отдохнуть'.

examples.text: Вы отдыхайте, а мы сами поедем.
examples.trans: You rest, and we'll go ourselves.
Everything is great, get some rest!
In the summer we vacation by the sea.
